statement: A function f of whole numbers is subadditive when f(a + b) is at most f(a) + f(b) for all whole numbers a and b. Define a function of such an f that gives true when f is subadditive and false when some a and b show it is not. It must decide for all whole numbers, however large. The program's value is the function.
origin: The triangle inequality |a + b| <= |a| + |b|, as subadditivity
